links.passage: Above fact highlight that application of small amounts of nutrient solution at frequent intervals proven better as it reduces deep percolation losses of applied nutrients as well as water (Souza, Folegatti, and Or 2009).
supporting_passages: Better understanding of nutrients dynamics in the soil under drip fertigation within the crop root zone is very useful for designing efficient fertigation systems.
links.inference_note: The frequent small-dose application described is the drip fertigation practice named in the preceding passage, and the cited claim is that it reduces deep percolation losses of water.

links.passage: Therefore, fertigation practice has shown to be a much better practice to fertilize crops that outcome quality produce, higher productivity and minimize the risk of environmental pollution through reduction in nutrient losses (Badr and Abou El-Yazied 2007) (Figure 2).

links.passage: Application of NPK nutrients through fertigation @ 125% of recommended dose resulted in higher plant height and number of leaves at 30, 50 and 70 days after sowing as well as higher leaf minerals (N, P and K) contents, fruit setting % age, fruit weight, number of fruits and fruits yield of cucumber (Mostafa, Zohair, and Abdishakur 2014).

links.passage: Similarly, fertigation practices involving 100% RDF containing MAP, multi K and urea increased tomato plant height, dry matter production, leaf area index, total chlorophyll content, number of fruits per plants, fruit weight and yield per plant tremendously (Kalanjiyam and Manickam 2015).
